mainTopic: Treating joined parts as separate, and how far the mother's שחיטה reaches: the fetus's limb in the debate between רבי מאיר and the חכמים, and a limb hanging from the animal
overview: This amud opens with the end of רבינא's rule: something that is going to be cut off is treated as already cut. That is why a fetus's foreleg and the rest of the fetus count as two separate pieces touching. The גמרא first suggests this follows only רבי מאיר, who says a too-long handle needs to be immersed only up to its final length. It then answers that even the רבנן agree that joined pieces of food count as separate pieces touching. After explaining why the משנה says 'he cut it off,' the גמרא turns to the חכמים's view. They hold that a slaughtered טרפה makes מוקדשין impure, and that the mother's שחיטה saves the fetus's limb from נבלה impurity, just as שחיטה saves a טרפה. רבא shows that the ברייתא recording the debate with רבי מאיר is missing lines, and a second ברייתא confirms the full order of the argument. ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן then disagree about whether the same מחלוקת covers a limb hanging from the animal itself. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains רבי יוחנן's distinction: a fetus's limb can go back into the womb, but a hanging limb can never be reattached. The amud ends with a challenge to רבי יוחנן from רבי מאיר's words in the ברייתא, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Whatever will be cut off counts as already cut
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבינא's principle: something that stands to be cut off is treated as if it were already cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Whatever is going to be cut off] is treated as if it were already cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבינא's statement that something which is going to be cut off is treated as already cut. He uses this to explain how the foreleg can pass טומאה to the fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The foreleg is going to be cut off, so it is viewed as already separated from the fetus. The place where they join therefore does not count as a hidden spot inside one body. Instead, they count as two separate items touching, so the foreleg can give טומאה to the fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: It is considered as if it were cut.
Anything that stands to be cut off (the beginning of רבינא's rule).

phrases.english: is considered as though it were cut.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּחָתוּךְ דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבינא's explanation, which began before this passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Something that stands to be cut off is treated as already cut, so the foreleg and the fetus count as separate items touching each other.

steps.title: Whose view is this? It seems to match רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion רבינא's principle follows and points to רבי מאיר in a משנה about immersing long handles.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? רבי מאיר's. As we learned in a משנה: any handles of vessels that are long, and that the owner plans to trim, only need to be immersed up to the length they will end up being. That is the statement of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion fits רבינא's principle. It answers רבי מאיר, and quotes a משנה as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a vessel needs every part under the water at once for its טבילה to work. רבי מאיר says the part of the handle that will be trimmed does not need to go in, because it already counts as cut off. That is exactly רבינא's idea, and this sets up the worry that only רבי מאיר holds it.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with whom? Whose opinion is this?
Handles of vessels.
He plans to cut them down later.
Immerses the vessel in a מקוה to make it טהור.
The point of the proper size, the length the handle will end up being.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi Meir,
as we learned: all handles of vessels
that are long and he plans to cut them down –
he immerses up to the place of the proper size,
phrases.notes: He means he only needs to dunk the handle up to where it will be trimmed.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source of רבינא's principle and suggests it matches only one תנא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that something standing to be cut off counts as already cut?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר, based on his ruling about long handles in מקואות.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's principle כל העומד לחתוך כחתוך דמי
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה מקואות 10:5, about immersing long handles

steps.title: The חכמים require immersing the whole handle
steps.stepSummary: The same משנה says the חכמים disagree and require the entire vessel, handle included, to be immersed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: not until he immerses all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה. The חכמים argue on רבי מאיר and say the whole handle must go into the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not treat the extra length as already cut off. So the משנה seems to show that רבינא's principle is a disputed view held only by רבי מאיר, and not by the חכמים. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Not until he immerses all of it.
Immersion in a מקוה for purification.

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying the handle is no longer part of the vessel in some other way. Their point is only that, for טבילה, the part that will be trimmed still counts as attached.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
not until he immerses all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: עַד שֶׁיַּטְבִּיל אֶת כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quoted משנה and shows that the רבנן disagree with רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: That רבינא's principle follows only רבי מאיר and not the רבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opinion of the חכמים in משנה מקואות 10:5

steps.title: Even the רבנן agree when it comes to food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even the רבנן treat pieces of food joined together as separate pieces touching each other, so רבינא's explanation works for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows the רבנן. Food that is joined together is considered as if it were already separated, and the pieces are touching each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבינא does not have to follow only רבי מאיר, because the רבנן agree when it comes to food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument in the משנה was about vessels. With food, everyone agrees that joined pieces count as separate pieces touching each other, so טומאה can pass from one to the other. The fetus and its foreleg are judged like food here, so they count as separate and touching even according to the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. Used to show a ruling can fit even the other opinion.
Connections between pieces of food.
They are considered as if they were separated.
They are touching one another.

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים about trimmed handles is about vessels. For food, everyone agrees that joined pieces are treated as separate pieces touching each other, so רבינא's explanation about the foreleg works even according to the רבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps רבינא's explanation in line with the majority view, by limiting the argument to vessels and showing that food follows its own rule.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows the Rabbis,
connections of foods
are considered as though they were separated,
and they are touching one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion from steps 2 and 3 that רבינא follows only רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the argument: the dispute is about vessels, but everyone agrees about food.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought that since the חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר about handles, רבינא's principle follows only רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the רבנן agree that joined pieces of food count as separate pieces touching each other, so רבינא's explanation fits everyone.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the idea that רבינא must follow רבי מאיר, not the dispute in the משנה itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof from vessels does not carry over to food, which follows its own rule.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'he cut it off' according to רבינא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבינא: the משנה's word 'חתכה' fits עולא's explanation, but seems unnecessary according to רבינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to עולא, that is why the משנה says 'he cut it off.' But according to רבינא, why does it say 'he cut it off'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that one word in the משנה, 'חתכה' (he cut it off), fits עולא well but seems pointless according to רבינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For עולא, the impurity comes at the moment the limb is cut off, so the cutting is essential. For רבינא, the limb and the fetus are like joined pieces of food, so the flesh would be impure even with no cutting at all. So why would the משנה mention the cutting?

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this works well (for one side, but not the other)
He cut it off (the foreleg that came out of the womb)
But (introduces the side that has a problem)

phrases.english: Granted, according to Ulla,
this is why the mishna teaches "he cut it off,"
but according to Ravina,
why does it say "he cut it off"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְעוּלָּא, הַיְינוּ דְּקָתָנֵי ״חֲתָכָהּ״, אֶלָּא לְרָבִינָא, מַאי ״חֲתָכָהּ״?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the גמרא has said רבינא's explanation works for everyone, it challenges him from the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's explanation that the limb is treated like joined food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the flesh would be impure even without cutting, the משנה's word 'חתכה' seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The word was repeated to match the first clause
steps.stepSummary: The משנה said 'חתכה' in the second clause only because it used that word in the first clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the first clause taught 'he cut it off,' the second clause also taught 'he cut it off.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'חתכה' in the second clause is there only to match the wording of the first clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first clause the cutting really matters, because the limb was cut off before the mother was slaughtered. The second clause simply kept the same wording, even though for רבינא the law would be the same without the cutting. So the word does not prove anything against רבינא.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because (it said it there, it also said it here)
The first clause of the משנה
The later clause of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The 'אַיְּידֵי' answer: a word in one clause can be there only to match the wording of another clause, so we should not learn a law from it.

phrases.english: Since it taught in the first clause "he cut it off,"
it also taught in the latter clause "he cut it off."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא ״חֲתָכָהּ״, תְּנָא נָמֵי סֵיפָא ״חֲתָכָהּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'חתכה' in the second clause is needed for the law, which would go against רבינא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word is only there to match the first clause, so רבינא's explanation stands.

steps.title: Can a slaughtered טרפה make things impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים's ruling, 'contact with a slaughtered טרפה,' and asks whether a slaughtered טרפה makes anything impure at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the חכמים say: contact with a slaughtered טרפה.' Does a slaughtered טרפה make things impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, where the חכמים say the flesh has 'contact with a slaughtered טרפה.' It asks how that could cause any impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טרפה that was slaughtered is not a נבלה, because its שחיטה keeps it from נבלה impurity. So it seems it should not make anything impure. Why would the חכמים describe the flesh with this impurity-sounding label?

keyTerms.meaning: Contact / touching (a type of impurity received by touching)
A fatally flawed animal that was properly slaughtered
Makes impure

steps.confusionAlert: A slaughtered טרפה is still forbidden to eat, but forbidden to eat is not the same as impure. The question here is only about impurity.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
contact with a slaughtered tereifa.
phrases.notes: The חכמים treat the limb that came out like a slaughtered טרפה, and the rest of the fetus touched it.

phrases.english: Does a slaughtered tereifa make things impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: טְרֵפָה שְׁחוּטָה מִי מְטַמְּיָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next part of the משנה: the חכמים's opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a slaughtered טרפה can make anything impure, as the חכמים's wording suggests.

steps.title: Yes: it makes holy sacrificial meat impure
steps.stepSummary: Yes. As אבוה דשמואל says, a slaughtered טרפה makes מוקדשין impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, like אבוה דשמואל, who said: a טרפה that was slaughtered makes מוקדשין impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers yes, using a ruling of אבוה דשמואל (שמואל's father).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slaughtered טרפה does not make ordinary food impure. But it does make holy sacrificial food (מוקדשין) impure. So 'contact with a slaughtered טרפה' is a real, though limited, status.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Holy items, such as sacrificial meat

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the חכמים's label has a practical meaning: the fetus's flesh would disqualify מוקדשין that it touches.

phrases.english: Yes, in accordance with Shmuel's father,
as Shmuel's father said:
a tereifa that one slaughtered
makes sacrificial items impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, כְּדַאֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A slaughtered טרפה makes מוקדשין impure, as אבוה דשמואל ruled.

steps.title: The חכמים's reasoning: שחיטה purifies, like with a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's reasoning for the חכמים: just as שחיטה makes a טרפה pure, the mother's שחיטה should make the fetus pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as we find that a טרפה's שחיטה makes it pure, so too the slaughter of the mother animal should make the fetus pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which gives the חכמים's reason. This sets up רבי מאיר's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים compare the two cases. A טרפה is forbidden to eat, yet its שחיטה still saves it from נבלה impurity. In the same way, the limb that came out is forbidden to eat, yet the mother's שחיטה should still save it from נבלה impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as we find (a comparison to a known case)
Makes it pure (here: keeps it from נבלה impurity)
Fetus

phrases.english: Just as we find with a tereifa
that its slaughter makes it pure,
so too, the slaughter of the animal
should make the fetus pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה מָצִינוּ בִּטְרֵפָה שֶׁשְּׁחִיטָתָהּ מְטַהַרְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the חכמים's view from the משנה, now giving their reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mother's שחיטה saves the fetus's limb from נבלה impurity, just as שחיטה saves a טרפה, even though both are forbidden to eat.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: then it should also be permitted to eat
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי מאיר's challenge: if the mother's שחיטה purified this limb, it should also permit eating it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי מאיר said to them: What made this limb pure from נבלה impurity? Its mother's שחיטה! If so, it should also permit it for eating!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with רבי מאיר's answer to the חכמים. He argues that their reasoning proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a טרפה, the animal's own שחיטה purifies it, and only its flaw keeps it forbidden. Here, the חכמים say the mother's שחיטה works on the limb. But רבי מאיר says that if the mother's שחיטה works on the limb, it should work fully and permit eating it too. Since everyone agrees the limb is forbidden, the mother's שחיטה must not work on it at all.

keyTerms.meaning: From the status (impurity) of a נבלה
The slaughter of its mother
It should permit it for eating

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's point: purity and permission to eat come from the same שחיטה. If the mother's שחיטה does not permit the limb for eating, it does not purify it either.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir said to them:
But what made this limb pure
from the impurity of a carcass?
The slaughter of its mother!
If so, it should permit it for eating!

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי מֵאִיר: וְכִי מִי טִיהֲרוֹ לְאֵבֶר זֶה מִידֵי נְבֵלָה?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חכמים's comparison to טרפה from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's comparison of the fetus's limb to a slaughtered טרפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the mother's שחיטה works on the limb enough to purify it, it should also permit eating it. But the limb is forbidden, so the comparison fails.

steps.title: The חכמים answer that שחיטה protects what is not its own body even more
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reply to רבי מאיר that שחיטה protects things that are not part of the animal's body more than its own body. They prove it from the משנה about cutting pieces from a fetus versus from the spleen or kidneys.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: שחיטה protects what is not its body much more than its own body. We learned: if someone cuts pieces from the fetus inside the animal, they may be eaten. If he cuts from the spleen or kidneys, they may not be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the חכמים's answer to רבי מאיר's challenge from step 10. They say the mother's שחיטה works even better on things that are not her own body, like a fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their proof: pieces cut from a fetus inside the mother become permitted when the mother is slaughtered. Pieces cut from her own spleen or kidneys stay forbidden. So שחיטה reaches the fetus in a way it does not reach her own cut-off parts. But this answer does not seem to fit רבי מאיר's question about eating, which sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: protects or saves (here, protects from נבלה status)
something that is not part of the animal's own body
the fetus inside the mother's womb
spleen
kidneys

steps.confusionAlert: If this answer seems not to fit רבי מאיר's question about eating, you are reading it correctly. The גמרא itself is about to ask 'what are they saying?'

phrases.english: They said to him: It protects much more
that which is not its body than its own body,
for we learned:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה at the start of this perek (68a).

phrases.aramaic: חוֹתֵךְ מִן הָעוּבָּר שֶׁבְּמֵעֶיהָ – מוּתָּר בַּאֲכִילָה,
phrases.english: One who cuts from the fetus inside her womb – it is permitted to eat,

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַטְּחוֹל וּמִן הַכְּלָיוֹת – אָסוּר בַּאֲכִילָה.
phrases.english: from the spleen or from the kidneys – it is forbidden to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: הַרְבֵּה מַצֶּלֶת עַל שֶׁאֵינוֹ גּוּפָהּ יוֹתֵר מִגּוּפָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים's quoted reply to רבי מאיר's challenge in step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof that שחיטה reaches a fetus more strongly than the mother's own body
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If שחיטה purifies the limb, it should also permit eating it (רבי מאיר)
steps.terutzMaskana: שחיטה works more strongly on what is not the mother's body, as the משנה about the fetus and the spleen shows

steps.title: What do the חכמים mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the חכמים's reply means, because it does not match רבי מאיר's challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops and asks what the חכמים's answer means. This sets up the next step, where the missing lines are filled in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר asked about eating, but the חכמים answered about 'its body versus not its body.' That answer only makes sense as a reply to a different argument, which the ברייתא does not show. So the גמרא asks for an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: what is he saying? (asking for the meaning of a statement)
what
is saying

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the חכמים's reply in step 11 answers the challenge in step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does 'it protects what is not its body more' answer רבי מאיר's point about eating?

steps.title: רבא fills in the missing lines: the proof from טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא is missing lines. רבי מאיר asked why the mother's שחיטה should purify the limb and not permit it. The חכמים answered that a טרפה proves it: its שחיטה makes it pure but does not permit eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said (some say it without a name): Lines are missing, and this is what it teaches. רבי מאיר said to them: What made this limb pure from נבלה? The mother's שחיטה? Then it should also permit eating it! They said to him: A טרפה proves it. Its שחיטה makes it pure from נבלה, but does not permit eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by saying the ברייתא left out part of the debate. He rebuilds the first missing exchange: the חכמים answer רבי מאיר from the case of a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a slaughtered טרפה, שחיטה makes the animal pure from נבלה but still does not let you eat it. So purity and permission to eat can be separate. The חכמים say the same is true of the fetus's limb: pure, but not permitted to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: something is missing, and this is what it teaches (the text is filled in)
without a name attached
limb
let a טרפה prove it (a case that shows the point)
it should permit it for eating

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that making something pure from נבלה and making it permitted to eat are two separate results of שחיטה.

phrases.english: Rava said, and some say it without a name:
Something is missing, and this is what it teaches,
Rabbi Meir said to them:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מִי טִהֲרוֹ לְאֵבֶר זֶה מִידֵּי נְבֵלָה?
phrases.english: But what made this limb pure from נבלה?
phrases.notes: 'This limb' is the fetus's leg that stuck out of the womb before the mother was slaughtered.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁחִיטַת אִמּוֹ, אִם כֵּן תַּתִּירֶנּוּ בַּאֲכִילָה!
phrases.english: The slaughter of its mother? If so, it should permit it for eating!
They said to him: A טרפה will prove it,
for its slaughter makes it pure from נבלה
and does not permit it for eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַסּוֹרֵי מְחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by filling in the missing part of the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Text is incomplete (חסורי מחסרא); missing exchange restored
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים answered רבי מאיר's eating question directly with 'not its body'
steps.terutzMaskana: First the חכמים answered with טרפה; the 'not its body' line answers a later objection
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is missing lines. The חכמים first answered רבי מאיר's question about eating from the case of a טרפה, whose שחיטה makes it pure but does not permit eating it. The 'not its body' line answers a later objection.

steps.title: רבי מאיר rejects the טרפה comparison
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that a טרפה is different. Its שחיטה purifies its own body, but that does not prove it can purify a limb that is not her body.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: No. If the שחיטה of a טרפה made it pure, that is something that is its own body. Should it make pure the limb, something that is not its body?
steps.whatsHappening: In the filled-in ברייתא, רבי מאיר pushes back on the טרפה proof. He says the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slaughtered טרפה is the very animal that was slaughtered, so of course its שחיטה affects it. The fetus's limb is a separate creature, so it may be outside the reach of the mother's שחיטה. This is the objection that the 'not its body' answer was really aimed at.

keyTerms.meaning: no, if... (pushing back on a comparison by showing a difference)
something that is her own body
should it make pure?

phrases.english: He said to them: No,

phrases.aramaic: אִם טִיהֲרָה שְׁחִיטַת טְרֵפָה אוֹתָהּ, דָּבָר שֶׁהִיא גּוּפָהּ,
phrases.english: if the slaughter of a טרפה made it pure, something that is its own body,

phrases.aramaic: תְּטַהֵר אֶת הָאֵבֶר דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ גּוּפָהּ?
phrases.english: should it make pure the limb, something that is not its body?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: לֹא, אִם טִיהֲרָה שְׁחִיטַת טְרֵפָה אוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי מאיר attacks the טרפה proof given in step 13
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טרפה is the slaughtered animal's own body; the fetus's limb is not, so the comparison fails

steps.title: The חכמים's answer now in its right place
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that שחיטה protects what is not its body even more than its own body. The proof is the משנה: cut pieces of a fetus are permitted, cut pieces of spleen or kidneys are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: שחיטה protects what is not its body much more than its own body. We learned: if someone cuts from the fetus inside her, it may be eaten. From the spleen or kidneys, it may not be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The same reply from step 11 is repeated, but now it answers the right point. It answers רבי מאיר's claim that the limb is 'not her body.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said 'not her body' makes שחיטה weaker. The חכמים show the opposite: a cut piece of the fetus becomes permitted through the mother's שחיטה. A cut piece of her own spleen does not. So 'not her body' is actually covered more strongly.

keyTerms.meaning: one who cuts (before the שחיטה)
permitted to eat
forbidden to eat

steps.whatToRemember: The full order of the debate is: רבי מאיר asks about eating, the חכמים answer from טרפה, רבי מאיר says a טרפה is her own body, and the חכמים reply that שחיטה protects what is not her body even more.

phrases.english: They said to him: It protects much more
that which is not its body than its own body,
for we learned:

phrases.aramaic: חוֹתֵךְ מִן הָעוּבָּר שֶׁבְּמֵעֶיהָ – מוּתָּר בַּאֲכִילָה,
phrases.english: One who cuts from the fetus inside her womb – it is permitted to eat,

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַטְּחוֹל וּמִן הַכְּלָיוֹת – אָסוּר בַּאֲכִילָה.
phrases.english: from the spleen or from the kidneys – it is forbidden to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: הַרְבֵּה מַצֶּלֶת עַל שֶׁאֵינוֹ גּוּפָהּ יוֹתֵר מִגּוּפָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי מאיר's objection in step 14; the reply from step 11 now placed where it belongs
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reverses the objection: being 'not its body' makes שחיטה's effect stronger, not weaker
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שחיטה cannot reach a limb that is not the mother's own body
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה shows שחיטה permits cut pieces of a fetus but not cut pieces of the mother's organs

steps.title: A ברייתא that has the fuller wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the exchange spelled out, just as רבא filled it in. רבי מאיר asks what purified the limb, the חכמים answer the mother's שחיטה, and the טרפה proof follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: רבי מאיר said to them: What made this limb pure from נבלה? They said to him: The slaughter of its mother. If so, it should permit it for eating! They said to him: A טרפה proves it. Its שחיטה makes it pure from נבלה but does not permit eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רבא's filling-in by quoting a ברייתא that actually has these lines written out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the חכמים openly say 'the slaughter of its mother,' and only then does רבי מאיר ask about eating. This matches the order רבא rebuilt in step 13, so his reading is confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: the slaughter of its mother
makes it pure
permits it
from the status of נבלה

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Rabbi Meir said to them:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מִי טִיהֲרוֹ לְאֵבֶר זֶה מִידֵּי נְבֵלָה?
phrases.english: But what made this limb pure from נבלה?
They said to him: The slaughter of its mother.
If so, it should permit it for eating!
They said to him: A טרפה will prove it,
for its slaughter makes it pure from נבלה
and does not permit it for eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's filling-in of the ברייתא in step 13
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the ברייתא is missing lines, and his order of the exchange
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that has the full exchange written out

steps.title: In the ברייתא, רבי מאיר says a טרפה only proves the case of its own body
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, רבי מאיר pushes back on the טרפה proof. A טרפה's שחיטה purifies its own body and a limb hanging from it, because those are its body. That does not show it can purify the fetus's limb, which is not its body.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The שחיטה of a טרפה purifies the animal and the limb hanging from it, because those are its own body. Does that mean it will purify the fetus, which is not its body?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 16 keeps going. It now states in its own words רבי מאיר's reply that רבא had filled in back in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר splits the cases into two groups: the animal's own body, and something that is not its body. The טרפה proof only covers the first group. So it cannot teach anything about the fetus's limb, which is in the second group. This ברייתא also adds the case of a limb hanging from the animal as part of 'its body'.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb that is partly cut off but still hangs from the animal
Something that is part of the animal's own body
Something that is not part of the animal's own body
It made pure, so it does not carry the טומאה of a נבלה

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר answering the חכמים inside the ברייתא.

phrases.english: If the slaughter of a טרפה purified the animal itself
and the limb dangling from it,
that is something which is its own body,
should it purify the fetus, which is not its body?
phrases.notes: He means the limb of the fetus that came out of the womb.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר להן: אם טיהרה שחיטת טרפה אותה ואת האבר המדולדל בה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 16. It shows the actual wording of רבי מאיר's reply that רבא had filled in back in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's proof from a טרפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טרפה only shows that שחיטה purifies the animal's own body. The fetus's limb is not its body, so the proof does not reach it.

steps.title: The חכמים say שחיטה protects what is not its body even more
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that שחיטה protects what is not the animal's body even more than its own body. They prove it from the משנה. Pieces cut from a fetus inside the womb are permitted after the mother's שחיטה. Pieces cut from the spleen or kidneys are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: שחיטה protects what is not its body much more than its own body. We learned in the משנה: If someone cuts from the fetus inside her, it is permitted to eat. If someone cuts from the spleen or kidneys, it is forbidden to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the חכמים's reply to רבי מאיר. It matches what was laid out in step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים take רבי מאיר's own split and turn it around. The משנה shows that the mother's שחיטה helps a fetus's cut pieces become permitted. It does not help her own cut organs. So 'not its body' is actually the stronger case. If שחיטה purifies her own body, it will surely purify the fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: Protects, shields from the טומאה of a נבלה
The fetus inside the mother's womb
Spleen
Kidneys

steps.whatToRemember: In this ברייתא, the חכמים hold that the mother's שחיטה purifies the fetus's limb. Their proof is that שחיטה helps what is not her body even more than her own body.

phrases.english: They said to him:
It protects what is not its body much more
than its own body,
for we have learned:
If one cuts from the fetus inside her,
it is permitted to eat;
from the spleen or from the kidneys,
it is forbidden to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמרו לו: הרבה מצלת על שאינו גופה יותר מגופה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי מאיר's challenge in step 17 and finishes the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reverses the distinction: the case that is not her body is stronger, not weaker
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר thought שחיטה works better on the animal's own body than on something that is not its body.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה shows that שחיטה works better on what is not its body. So the fetus's limb is purified.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the same מחלוקת applies to a limb hanging from the animal
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says that רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about a hanging limb of the animal the same way they argue about the fetus's limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: Just as there is a מחלוקת about fetuses, so there is a מחלוקת about limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion opens. ריש לקיש tells us how far the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and the חכמים reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was about a fetus's limb that came out of the womb. ריש לקיש says the same argument also covers a limb partly cut off from the animal that still hangs on it. The question is whether the animal's שחיטה keeps that limb from the טומאה of a נבלה. In his view, רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree here too.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute between תנאים
Fetuses, here meaning a fetus's limb that came out of the womb
Limbs, here meaning limbs hanging from the animal itself

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Just as there is a dispute about fetuses,
so there is a dispute about limbs.
phrases.notes: He means limbs still hanging from the animal itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש: כמחלוקת בעוברין כך מחלוקת באיברין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא is finished, this opens a new question about how far its מחלוקת reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and the חכמים covers both a fetus's limb and a limb hanging from the animal.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the מחלוקת is only about a fetus's limb
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the מחלוקת to a fetus's limb. For a limb hanging from the animal itself, everyone agrees that שחיטה treats it as if it already fell off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The מחלוקת is about a limb of a fetus. But for a limb of the animal, everyone agrees that שחיטה makes it 'fallen'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with ריש לקיש about how far the מחלוקת goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, only the fetus's limb is in dispute. A limb hanging from the animal is treated by שחיטה as if it had already dropped off. So the שחיטה does not protect it from the טומאה of a נבלה, and both רבי מאיר and the חכמים agree on this.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Fallen: treated as if it had already dropped off the animal
A limb of the animal itself, as opposed to a limb of the fetus

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of limbs. 'אבר דעובר' is the fetus's limb, and that is in dispute. 'אבר דבהמה' is the mother's own hanging limb, and רבי יוחנן says everyone agrees about it.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש says the מחלוקת also covers a limb hanging from the animal. רבי יוחנן says it covers only a fetus's limb. For the animal's own hanging limb, everyone agrees שחיטה makes it 'fallen'.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The dispute is about a limb of a fetus,
but about a limb of an animal,
everyone agrees
that slaughter makes it 'fallen'.
phrases.notes: The hanging limb is treated as if it already dropped off, so the שחיטה does not save it from נבלה טומאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבי יוחנן אמר: מחלוקת באבר דעובר, אבל באבר דבהמה דברי הכל שחיטה עושה ניפול
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different view from ריש לקיש's in step 19 about how far the מחלוקת reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a fetus's limb is in dispute. For a limb hanging from the animal, everyone agrees that שחיטה makes it 'fallen' and does not purify it.

steps.title: Why the fetus's limb is different from the animal's hanging limb
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains רבי יוחנן's view of the חכמים. The fetus's limb can be fixed by going back into the womb, but a limb hanging from the animal cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: Why does רבי יוחנן say the חכמים treat these two limbs differently? The fetus's limb that came out can be fixed by putting it back inside. The limb hanging from the animal has no fix like that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind רבי יוחנן's statement from step 20. That statement said the חכמים argue only about a fetus's limb and agree about a limb hanging from the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fetus's limb that came out of the womb can still go back in, so it is not fully cut off from the mother's שחיטה. A limb hanging from the animal's own body can never be reattached. So the שחיטה treats it as if it already fell off, and it is not purified.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
According to the view of the חכמים
A fix, a way to repair the situation
Going back, returning to its place

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a clear rule for why the חכמים can purify one limb and not the other. Something that can still return to its place stays connected. Something that never can is treated as already fallen off.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yochanan
according to the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוחנן's statement in step 20: the חכמים purify the fetus's limb but not a limb hanging from the animal.

phrases.english: This one has a fix by going back in,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the fetus's limb, which can be pushed back into the womb.

phrases.english: but this one has no fix by going back.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבי יוחנן's distinction in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the mother's שחיטה purifies the fetus's limb because it can be returned to the womb. A limb hanging from the animal cannot be reattached, so it is not purified.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי מאיר's words about the hanging limb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי מאיר in the ברייתא again. He says the שחיטה purifies a limb hanging from the animal, which seems to go against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises an objection. רבי מאיר said to the חכמים: No! The שחיטה of a טרפה purifies the animal and the limb hanging from it, because those are its own body. Does that mean it should purify the fetus's limb, which is not its body?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. It brings back רבי מאיר's words from the ברייתא in step 17, this time for a new purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר takes it for granted that the שחיטה purifies a limb hanging from the animal. The חכמים did not argue with that point. But רבי יוחנן said everyone agrees the hanging limb is treated as if it fell off and is not purified, so the ברייתא seems to go against him.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a deadly defect
A limb that is hanging loose but still attached
Something that is part of its own body
Fetus

steps.confusionAlert: In step 17 these same words were part of the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים. Here the גמרא quotes them only to pull out one assumption: the hanging limb is purified. It uses that assumption to challenge רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Meir said to them: No,
if the slaughter of a tereifa purified
itself and the limb hanging from it,
something that is its body,
should it purify the fetus,
phrases.notes: He means the fetus's limb that came out of the womb.

phrases.english: something that is not its body?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבי יוחנן position that step 21 just explained, using the ברייתא from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that everyone agrees a limb hanging from the animal is treated as fallen off and is not purified by שחיטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבי מאיר takes it for granted that the שחיטה purifies the hanging limb, and the חכמים do not argue. That suggests the hanging limb is purified, against רבי יוחנן.
